newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call rate rises as banks position long-term.
newsitem.headline: Manila call rate rises as banks position long-term.

text.p: * Interbank call loan rate up at 11.71875 pct

Philippine overnight money rose to 11.71875 percent on Tuesday from the previous 11.125 percent as banks positioned in long-term instruments in anticipation of a further decline in rates, traders said.

One trader said many domestic banks were buying Treasury bills to park their funds in, driving rates in the secondary market lower. The T-bill buying left many banks short to cover their short-term requirements.
Quarterly tax remittances also siphoned off about 6.0 billion pesos from the system, he added.
Another trader said foreign funds, on the other hand, have been withdrawing due to falling interest rates.
Turnover in the interbank market was moderate at 20.938 billion pesos with done rates ranged from 11.125 to 12.6875 percent.
On the other hand, secondary T-bill rates went down as compared with their corresponding auction rates as buyers swamped the market.

Three-month bills were being bid with an effective yield of 11.1 to 11.2 percent, down from yesterday's auction average of 11.33 percent. "There were no sellers of three-month bills," one trader said.
The six-month bills were being bid at 11.5, while the one-year bills were at 12.4 to 12.5 percent.
